remaining_external.evidence: Single-product probe of frozen record 228823 through the closure cleaner+enricher on the closure code. The Vitamin A row is fully retained and assessed: cleaner_row_role 'active_scorable', score_eligible_by_cleaner true, canonical_id 'vitamin_a', quantity 3000.0 mcg, dose_class 'therapeutic_mass'. Its typed dose assessment reads: conversion_rule_id 'vitamin_a_unknown', conversion_status 'converted', normalized_value 3000.0 normalized_unit 'mcg', ul_assessment_status 'unresolved_form', ul_value null, ul_unit 'mcg RAE', pct_ul null, reason_code 'unknown_vitamin_form', readiness 'incomplete'.
remaining_external.failure_path: The label declares Vitamin A with no form (no 'Form: as ...' note, so retinol vs beta-carotene is undetermined). Without a form the engine cannot select the retinol-RAE upper limit, so it refuses to make a UL claim and marks the dose assessment incomplete. That single incomplete assessment is what lands 'ingredientRows[5]' in assessment_readiness.dose.incomplete_source_row_refs (27 of 28 material rows assessed) and blocks the product on the completeness gate.
remaining_external.engineering_conclusion: Correctly conservative, not a defect. The quantity, unit and %DV are all preserved and mutually consistent (3000 mcg vs 334%DV and 3417 mcg vs 380%DV both resolve against a 900 mcg RAE reference). No amount is discarded and no form is invented. The only missing input is the label's own form declaration, which engineering cannot supply.
remaining_external.recommended_correction: Reviewed form-provenance determination for the Vitamin A row from the printed label/manufacturer source. Do NOT relax the form requirement and do NOT default to retinol.
remaining_external.products_affected_readiness: all five Bulk 1340 SKUs carry incomplete_source_row_refs ['ingredientRows[5]'] (= the Vitamin A row)

remaining_external.item: Folate parent-total/form-breakdown double count (3 residual shapes)
remaining_external.pre_existing_proof: Folate flags are byte-identical at base 124982a0 and at 095d27a1 for all three: pct_ul 161.55/257.29/140.79, penalized True/True/False, state confirmed_over_threshold. The remediation neither introduced nor changed them.
remaining_external.blast_radius: Corpus-wide there are 58 folate dose-safety flags. 55 are correctly reconciled as parent-total + form-breakdown duplicates (state not_applicable, reason folate_parent_total_plus_form_breakdown_duplicate). Only 3 are unreconciled.

the_three_shapes.source_shape: Folic Acid 1333 mcg DFE [333%DV] with one nested child Folic Acid 800 mcg
the_three_shapes.why_unreconciled: The declared total row is named 'Folic Acid', which is not in _FOLATE_PARENT_NAMES ({folate, vitamin b9 folate, vitamin b9}), so the recognizer treats both rows as forms and sums them (161.5%).
the_three_shapes.material_impact: low - the product is independently over-UL on three other nutrients and remains CAUTION either way

the_three_shapes.source_shape: Folate 1667 mcg DFE [417%DV] with one nested child Folic Acid 400 mcg
the_three_shapes.why_unreconciled: 1667 = 1000 mcg L-5-MTHF (1000 mcg DFE) + 400 mcg folic acid x1.7 (680 mcg DFE); the nested child is a partial breakdown already inside the declared total, but the recognizer requires the form rows to FULLY account for the parent (|parent - form_sum| within tolerance), which a subset cannot satisfy. Engine sums 1667 + 680 = 2347 -> 140.8%.
the_three_shapes.material_impact: highest of the three - the folate flag is the product's ONLY dose-safety finding, on an otherwise 85.9-scoring prenatal, so this is a false-positive over-limit state. It is NOT penalized (penalized=false) and the product is not quarantined, but it does set safety_verdict CAUTION.

the_three_shapes.source_shape: Folate 725/667 mcg DFE with TWO sibling children Folic Acid 435 mcg and Folic Acid 400 mcg
the_three_shapes.why_unreconciled: The two sibling children are the same declared form split across serving-size variants (DSLD emits one row per variant here, whereas sibling products emit one row carrying both variants). Both are converted (x1.7 x2 servings = 1479 and 1360) and SUMMED to 2839 against a parent of 1450, giving 4289 mcg DFE total -> 257.3%, penalized critical.
the_three_shapes.material_impact: low - independently over-UL on niacin and magnesium, so the product remains correctly quarantined/gated regardless

remaining_external.recommended_fix_shape: Complete the existing parent-total + form-breakdown contract rather than widen it to other nutrients: (a) recognise a declared-total row by exposure basis / DFE unit rather than by a parent-name vocabulary that omits 'Folic Acid'; (b) treat a nested form row of the same canonical nutrient as part of the declared total even when it is a SUBSET of it; (c) collapse sibling form rows that carry the same form name and basis to one exposure instead of summing them. Each sub-change flips a Safety outcome for a named product, so it belongs in one reviewed, tested change with these three as its fixtures.
why_not_fixed_in_this_closure: It is pre-existing behaviour, not a regression of this remediation (identical at base), so it is outside the remediation's regression responsibility in the same way the static-audit finding is.
It is a change to Safety semantics in the module whose own docstring states that widening the rule 'is a separate, validated change'.

Three structurally different signatures require three separate justifications; two of them sit within 0.05 percentage points of the existing reconciliation tolerance (228823 passes at 26/1334 = 1.95% against a ~2% limit), so an opportunistic edit risks silently changing which products trip a UL gate.
No product's disposition is masked either way: 201420 and 243808 are independently and genuinely over-UL, and 246430's flag is informational (not penalized) with the product still scored.

standardization_marker_review.rule: enhanced_normalizer._is_standardization_marker_row (+ _parent_is_standardized_botanical_extract): a nested row with a positive mcg/mg quantity whose parent name is a standardized botanical extract AND whose parent has a declared mass is a standardization MARKER of that parent, not an independent active.
standardization_marker_review.verdict: structurally correct and retained; no narrowing required
standardization_marker_review.why_structural: The predicate keys on nesting + a dosed parent + parent-naming semantics + a declared constituent quantity. It contains no product-ID or nutrient allowlist, and there is an explicit negative control (a nested constituent under a non-standardized extract stays scoreable).

standardization_marker_review.conclusion: Every affected constituent is a percentage disclosure of a dosed standardized extract on the same label (the parent's % note matches the child amount exactly: 3% of 100 mg = 3 mg, 6% of 100 mg = 6 mg, etc.). De-eligibilising the constituent while the parent keeps the dose is consistent with the scoring model and with the structural treatment already accepted for omega constituents. Safety is unaffected in all five products: every Safety field, signal and verdict is byte-identical between arms. The three non-target products move by +1.9 / +1.9 / +0.2 points, all tier-preserving.
standardization_marker_review.regression_added: scripts/tests/test_standardization_marker_generalization.py (5 tests) pins the non-target cases, the preserved disclosure quantities, the parent-keeps-the-dose property, and the non-standardized-extract negative control.
